annotator.notes: Student initially confuses the area of the L-shape with the area of the largest square minus the smallest square. Tutor guides them to decompose the shape.

task_context.reference_solution:
The $\text L$-shaped region is made up of two rectangles with area $3\times 1=3$ plus the corner square with area $1\times 1=1,$ so the area of the $\text L$-shaped figure is $2\times 3+1=\boxed{7}.$

OR

$\text{Square }FECG-\text{Square }FHIJ=4\times 4-3\times 3 =16-9=\boxed{7}.$

OR

The $\text L$-shaped region can be decomposed into a $4\times 1$ rectangle and a $3\times 1$ rectangle. So the total area is $\boxed{7}.$

Exactly. You need to account for all the non-shaded areas. Alternatively, you could try to break the $\text L$-shaped region into smaller, simpler rectangles. Which approach do you think would be easier?

Let me try breaking it into rectangles. There's a vertical rectangle on the left and a horizontal one on the bottom. The vertical one is $4$ high and $1$ wide, so area is $4$. The horizontal one is $3$ wide and $1$ high, so area is $3$. $4 + 3 = 7$. Is it 7?
